summary: An image CDN for your own sites without writing an image processor: originals in S3-compatible storage, imgproxy resizing and converting on request by signed URL, a cache in front, and a helper that emits srcset for every image. Video and the media library stay with the vendor.

stack.why: rule zero: do not write an image processor

stack.choice: Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2 or MinIO
stack.why: originals as objects, keyed by content hash
transforms are cheap once, expensive always

prerequisites.name: Node.js 22 or newer
prerequisites.why: Everything in this build runs on it: the server, the scripts, the tests.
prerequisites.get: Download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, or install with your package manager (brew install node, or nvm install 22). Restart the terminal afterwards.

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: An S3-compatible bucket with access keys
prerequisites.get: Cloudflare R2: dashboard > R2 > Create bucket > Manage R2 API Tokens. Backblaze B2: Buckets > Create, then App Keys. Note endpoint, bucket, key id and secret.
prerequisites.cost: cents to a few dollars a month

prerequisites.name: A small always-on server (VPS)
prerequisites.why: This needs one process running all the time with a public address. imgproxy needs a box; 2 GB of RAM is comfortable.
prerequisites.get: Hetzner Cloud (from about 4 EUR), DigitalOcean or Fly.io. Ubuntu 24.04, the smallest size. You need SSH access and a public IP. Only needed for the deploy phase; develop locally first.

prerequisites.name: A domain or subdomain
prerequisites.get: Register at Cloudflare Registrar, Porkbun or Namecheap, or use a subdomain of one you already own. You add one DNS record in the deploy phase.
prerequisites.cost: roughly $10 a year, or free on an existing domain

prerequisites.name: Caddy on the server
prerequisites.why: Automatic HTTPS in front of the Node process. Without TLS the browser features this relies on (and your visitors' trust) do not work.
prerequisites.get: On the VPS: follow the install steps at caddyserver.com/docs/install for Ubuntu. One Caddyfile with your domain and a reverse_proxy line is the whole config.
prerequisites.verify: caddy version prints a version on the server

prerequisites.name: imgproxy signing key and salt
prerequisites.why: Unsigned URLs would let anyone resize anything through your box.

env.name: UPLOAD_TOKEN
env.where: Bearer token for the upload endpoint.

env.name: IMG_URL
env.where: Public base of the image domain.

phases.title: Originals
phases.goal: Upload behind a token, content-hash keys, sniffed, capped, EXIF stripped, never overwritten.

steps.do: The upload endpoint with sharp for sniffing and EXIF stripping
commands: mkdir imgcdn && cd imgcdn && git init && npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module && npm install @aws-sdk/client-s3@3 sharp@0.35.3

steps.do: Store under sha256 of the bytes; refuse non-images and files over the cap

check: Two uploads of the same file store once
The stored file has no GPS EXIF

phases.title: Transforms
phases.goal: imgproxy with the bucket as source, signed URLs, auto WebP and AVIF.

steps.do: docker-compose.yml for imgproxy with S3 source and signing enabled
A helper img(key, width, height, format) building signed URLs

check: One original serves at three widths in the browser's preferred format

phases.title: Cache
phases.goal: Long cache headers, a cache in front, purge by key.

steps.do: Cache-Control on transforms; Cloudflare or Caddy cache

check: The second request is served by the cache
Purge makes the next request miss

phases.title: Responsive helper
phases.goal: srcset and sizes for every image in your site.

steps.do: A function producing srcset and sizes
A build step replacing plain img tags in your site

check: A phone loads the smallest sufficient image; a desktop the largest

phases.title: Operate
phases.goal: Lifecycle rules, memory limits, healthz, backups of the key index.

steps.do: imgproxy memory limits and /healthz; bucket lifecycle rules
README with the signing scheme and where originals live

check: imgproxy survives a 50 MB hostile image
The README reaches a served image

phases.title: Serve several sites

steps.do: Per-site key prefixes and upload tokens
Bandwidth and transform counts per site from the cache logs

check: Two sites upload to separate prefixes

product.outcome: Image delivery for all your sites at object-storage prices, with video honestly left out.

operations.backup: Originals are the asset: enable bucket versioning or replicate to a second bucket.
operations.monitoring: Uptime on img domain and imgproxy memory.
operations.incident: Rotate IMGPROXY_KEY; all old URLs stop, so regenerate.

notIncluded: Video, the media library, AI tagging, upload widgets: the $99.
after: Direct-to-bucket presigned uploads from the browser
